TODAY
The shipped MachineList, redrawn from source at its real values. One vertical list, constrained to max-w-4xl, holding only machines. Devices connected to the console have no home anywhere.

PROPOSED
Two rails on one axis. The subtitle does the terminology work: devices are where you are working FROM, machines are what you work ON. Rails take the full panel width — max-w-4xl is what makes the current list feel thin.

The lit screen is the lease. Only the device in control gets a lit silhouette — state as form, not just another pill.

Machines deliberately do NOT wear device silhouettes: a headless VPS is not a laptop, and reusing the frames would flatten the exact distinction this surface exists to make. They share the card grammar and the same body/rim tokens instead. The one exception is This computer, which genuinely is both.
Cards keep their 268px width on a phone and the rail becomes a swipe. Turning them back into full-width rows would land exactly where the current list is.

A is drawn in Proposed because it is what you asked for and it reads well on touch. B is worth a look if the device count usually sits at two or three — the rail leaves a lot of air there. C answers a question the cards cannot, so it belongs beside them rather than instead of them.
